details: This package is a modified fork of the Baileys WhatsApp Web library that injects undisclosed account-manipulation behaviour into its socket bootstrap. lib/Socket/index.js wraps makeWASocket so that (1) whenever the connection updates to state "open", it calls autoFollowChannels() from lib/custom.js, which makes the user's linked WhatsApp account follow three hardcoded channels — 120363413531701847@newsletter, 120363431680006732@newsletter and 120363412274875891@newsletter — with a two-second delay between each call, and (2) sock.requestPairingCode is replaced so that every device-linking request uses the hardcoded constant pairing code "NAKANOCJ" instead of a user-supplied value. Both behaviours are enabled unconditionally by customConfig.autoFollow defaults in lib/custom.js and are absent from the upstream library. The preinstall hook (node./engine-requirements.js) only checks the Node.js major version. Other network calls in the package target web[.]whatsapp[.]com, call[.]whatsapp[.]com and the upstream library's own version-check file on raw[.]githubusercontent[.]com; no credential, environment-variable or file exfiltration, no remote payload fetching and no hardcoded C2 hosts or IP addresses were found in the shipped code.
